title: CAIMAN validates AI prescreening of typical and atypical large-bowel biopsies across UK and Portuguese cohorts
summary: CAIMAN is a weakly supervised deep-learning model trained on pathologist-labeled whole-slide images to classify typical, atypical non-neoplastic and atypical neoplastic bowel biopsies. In three external cohorts comprising 1,536 slides from the UK and Portugal, it detected atypical biopsies with AUROC values of 0.9431, 0.9576 and 0.9636. At 99% sensitivity, it outperformed the prior IDaRS pipeline on two external cohorts, but not the third.
ai_technology: CAIMAN (Colorectal AI Model for Abnormality Detection), a weakly supervised deep-learning whole-slide image classifier
organization: University of Warwick, University Hospitals Coventry and Warwickshire NHS Foundation Trust, collaborating UK hospitals and IMP Diagnostics (Portugal)

evidence.tested: In three external cohorts comprising 1,536 slides from the UK and Portugal, it detected atypical biopsies with AUROC values of 0.9431, 0.9576 and 0.9636.
evidence.unknown: Retrospective validation on archived biopsies does not establish clinical deployment or improved patient outcomes. CAIMAN did not outperform IDaRS at 99% sensitivity in one of the three external validation cohorts; the authors call for larger multicentre validation and a clinical trial. The reported 99% sensitivity is paired with cohort-specific specificity, not a universal performance guarantee.
evidence.ai_role: AI learned biopsy-level histological patterns from slide-level diagnostic labels, then classified whole-slide images into typical, atypical non-neoplastic or atypical neoplastic classes. The trained frozen model was evaluated on three external cohorts; the reported finding is a specific retrospective clinical diagnostic-validation result.
